questions.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations 

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x-y=-6 \\ \,\,\,x+y=7.\end{aligned}
$$

According to Cramer's rule, the unknown $y$ can be written as $y=\frac{{D}_{y}}{|\begin{aligned}2 & \,\,-1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|}$, where ${D}_{y}=$
questions.worked_solution:
We are given the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x-y=-6 \\ \,\,\,x+y=7.\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}2 & \,\,-1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to construct ${D}_{y}$, we replace the second column of the coefficient matrix by the right-hand side column of the given system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{y} & =|\begin{aligned}2 & \,\,-6 \\ 1 & 7\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Let $⟨-1,y⟩$ be the solution of the system of equations below. 

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x+ky=-4 \\ 3x-4y=5.\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following equations could be solved to find the value of $k?$

- $|\begin{aligned}2 & k \\ 3 & -4\end{aligned}|=-2|\begin{aligned}-4 & k \\ 5 & -4\end{aligned}|$
- $|\begin{aligned}2 & k \\ 3 & -4\end{aligned}|=|\begin{aligned}-4 & k \\ 5 & -4\end{aligned}|$
- $|\begin{aligned}2 & k \\ 3 & -4\end{aligned}|=-|\begin{aligned}-4 & k \\ 5 & -4\end{aligned}|$
questions.worked_solution:
The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}2 & k \\ 3 & -4\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

According to Cramer's rule, the value of $x$ is given by $x=\frac{{D}_{x}}{D},$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{x} & =|\begin{aligned}-4 & k \\ 5 & -4\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{D}_{x}}{D} \\ -1 & =\frac{|\begin{aligned}-4 & k \\ 5 & -4\end{aligned}|}{|\begin{aligned}2 & k \\ 3 & -4\end{aligned}|} \\ |\begin{aligned}2 & k \\ 3 & -4\end{aligned}| & =-|\begin{aligned}-4 & k \\ 5 & -4\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

So, the correct answer is "III only".

questions.problem:
Let $⟨x,-2⟩$ be the solution of the system of equations below. 

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-y=2 \\ 2x+y=k\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following equations could be solved to find the value of $k?$

- $|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & k\end{aligned}|=-6$
- $|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & k\end{aligned}|=-12$
- $|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & k\end{aligned}|=3$
questions.worked_solution:
The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =1+2 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

According to Cramer's rule, the value of $y$ is given by $y=\frac{{D}_{y}}{D},$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{y} & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & k\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{{D}_{y}}{D} \\ -2 & =\frac{|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & k\end{aligned}|}{3} \\ |\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & k\end{aligned}| & =-6\end{aligned}
$$

So, the correct answer is "I only".

questions.problem:
Let $⟨-1,y⟩$ be the solution of the system of equations below. 

$$
{\begin{aligned}3x+5y=k \\ 2x-y=-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following equations could be solved to find the value of $k?$

- $|\begin{aligned}k & 5 \\ -4 & -1\end{aligned}|=-13$
- $|\begin{aligned}k & 5 \\ -4 & -1\end{aligned}|=-1$
- $|\begin{aligned}k & 5 \\ -4 & -1\end{aligned}|=13$
questions.worked_solution:
The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}3 & 5 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-3-10 \\  & -13.\end{aligned}
$$

According to Cramer's rule, the value of $x$ is given by $x=\frac{{D}_{x}}{D},$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{x} & =|\begin{aligned}k & 5 \\ -4 & -1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{D}_{x}}{D} \\ -1 & =\frac{|\begin{aligned}k & 5 \\ -4 & -1\end{aligned}|}{-13} \\ |\begin{aligned}k & 5 \\ -4 & -1\end{aligned}| & =(-1)(-13) \\ |\begin{aligned}k & 5 \\ -4 & -1\end{aligned}| & =13\end{aligned}
$$

So, the correct answer is "III only".

questions.problem:
Let $⟨-4,y⟩$ be the solution of the system of equations below. 

$$
{\begin{aligned}9x+11y=-14 \\ 6x-ky=-34.\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following equations could be solved to find the value of $k?$

- $|\begin{aligned}-14 & 11 \\ -34 & -k\end{aligned}|=-4|\begin{aligned}9 & 11 \\ 6 & -k\end{aligned}|$
- $|\begin{aligned}-14 & 1 \\ -34 & -k\end{aligned}|=4|\begin{aligned}9 & 11 \\ 6 & -k\end{aligned}|$
- $-4|\begin{aligned}-14 & 11 \\ -34 & -k\end{aligned}|=|\begin{aligned}9 & 11 \\ 6 & -k\end{aligned}|$
questions.worked_solution:
The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}9 & 11 \\ 6 & -k\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

According to Cramer's rule, the value of $x$ is given by $x=\frac{{D}_{x}}{D},$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{x} & =|\begin{aligned}-14 & 11 \\ -34 & -k\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{D}_{x}}{D} \\ -4 & =\frac{|\begin{aligned}-14 & 11 \\ -34 & -k\end{aligned}|}{|\begin{aligned}9 & 11 \\ 6 & -k\end{aligned}|} \\ -4|\begin{aligned}9 & 11 \\ 6 & -k\end{aligned}| & =|\begin{aligned}-14 & 11 \\ -34 & -k\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

So, the correct answer is "I only".

questions.problem:
Let $⟨x,-3⟩$ be the solution of the system of equations below. 

$$
{\begin{aligned}5x-y=k \\ -2x+4y=-12\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following equations could be solved to find the value of $k?$

- $|\begin{aligned}5 & k \\ -2 & -12\end{aligned}|=-6$
- $|\begin{aligned}5 & k \\ -2 & -12\end{aligned}|=-54$
- $|\begin{aligned}5 & k \\ -2 & -12\end{aligned}|=18$
questions.worked_solution:
The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}5 & -1 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =20-2 \\  & =18.\end{aligned}
$$

According to Cramer's rule, the value of $y$ is given by $y=\frac{{D}_{y}}{D},$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{y} & =|\begin{aligned}5 & k \\ -2 & -12\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{{D}_{y}}{D} \\ -3 & =\frac{|\begin{aligned}5 & k \\ -2 & -12\end{aligned}|}{18} \\ |\begin{aligned}5 & k \\ -2 & -12\end{aligned}| & =-54\end{aligned}
$$

So, the correct answer is "II only".
